Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

downhearted adjective

also dejected, depressed, downcast, be downhearted, feel down and out, dispirited, low (in spirits)

classical

Traupman 151
Lewis & Short s.v. dēmittō: “Trop. Downcast, dejected, dispirited, low (freq.)”
Traupman 302

dēmissus, dēmissa, dēmissum

declension

downcast, dejected

Other words

  • abjectus, abjecta, abjectum — downcast, depressed

    declension · also used · classical · Traupman 151

  • animō perculsō et abjectō esse — to be crushed and downhearted

    also used · classical · Cic. Att. 3.2: ita sum animō perculsō et abjectō (Lewis & Short); Traupman 151

    Traupman gives the two halves: animō perculsō esse, be downhearted; abjectō animō esse, be depressed.

  • jaceō, jacēre, jacuī — to lie low, be downcast

    verb, second conjugation · also used · classical · Traupman 151

  • īnfrāctum animum gerere — to feel crushed, down and out

    also used · classical · Liv. 7.31.6: īnfrāctōs animōs gerere (Lewis & Short); Traupman 152

See also depression, sad, gloomy.
